content: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your physician. If you are prescribed extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the entire dose at once, increasing the likelihood of side effects. To maximize the benefits of this medication, take it consistently at the same time(s) each day as instructed. Adhere strictly to your prescribed dosing schedule. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or changes in weight. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, this medication may rarely cause serious, and sometimes fatal, complications due to blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco products while on this medication. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone or are planning to undergo surgery, or if you will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially if you are taking an estrogen-containing product. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin or face (melasma), which can be exacerbated by sunlight. Limit your exposure to sunlight, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, which could potentially impact their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes effectively. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help prevent or control these conditions. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving crossword puzzles) to help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercises, quit smoking, limit alcohol consumption, and eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
